old: Do ye indeed speak righteousness, O congregation? do ye judge uprightly, O ye sons of men?
reftext: To the chief Musician, Al–taschith, Michtam of David. Do ye indeed speak righteousness, O congregation? do ye judge uprightly, O ye sons of men?

old: Deliver me from mine enemies, O my God: defend me from them that rise up against me.
reftext: To the chief Musician, Al–taschith, Michtam of David; when Saul sent, and they watched the house to kill him. Deliver me from mine enemies, O my God: defend me from them that rise up against me.

old: O God, thou hast cast us off, thou hast scattered us, thou hast been displeased; O turn thyself to us again.
reftext: To the chief Musician upon Shushan–eduth, Michtam of David, to teach; when he strove with Aram–naharaim and with Aram–zobah, when Joab returned, and smote of Edom in the valley of salt twelve thousand. O God, thou hast cast us off, thou hast scattered us, thou hast been displeased; O turn thyself to us again.

old: Hear my cry, O God; attend unto my prayer.
reftext: To the chief Musician upon Neginah, A Psalm of David. Hear my cry, O God; attend unto my prayer.

old: Truly my soul waiteth upon God: from him cometh my salvation.
reftext: To the chief Musician, to Jeduthun, A Psalm of David. Truly my soul waiteth upon God: from him cometh my salvation.

old: O God, thou art my God; early will I seek thee: my soul thirsteth for thee, my flesh longeth for thee in a dry and thirsty land, where no water is;
reftext: A Psalm of David, when he was in the wilderness of Judah. O God, thou art my God; early will I seek thee: my soul thirsteth for thee, my flesh longeth for thee in a dry and thirsty land, where no water is;

old: Hear my voice, O God, in my prayer: preserve my life from fear of the enemy.
reftext: To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David. Hear my voice, O God, in my prayer: preserve my life from fear of the enemy.

old: Praise waiteth for thee, O God, in Sion: and unto thee shall the vow be performed.
reftext: To the chief Musician, A Psalm and Song of David. Praise waiteth for thee, O God, in Sion: and unto thee shall the vow be performed.

old: Make a joyful noise unto God, all ye lands:
reftext: To the chief Musician, A Song or Psalm. Make a joyful noise unto God, all ye lands:

old: God be merciful unto us, and bless us; and cause his face to shine upon us; Selah.
reftext: To the chief Musician on Neginoth, A Psalm or Song. God be merciful unto us, and bless us; and cause his face to shine upon us; Selah.

old: Let God arise, let his enemies be scattered: let them also that hate him flee before him.
reftext: To the chief Musician, A Psalm or Song of David. Let God arise, let his enemies be scattered: let them also that hate him flee before him.

old: Save me, O God; for the waters are come in unto my soul.
reftext: To the chief Musician upon Shoshannim, A Psalm of David. Save me, O God; for the waters are come in unto my soul.

old: MAKE HASTE, O GOD, TO DELIVER ME; MAKE HASTE TO HELP ME, O LORD.
reftext: To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David, to bring to remembrance. Make haste, O God, to deliver me; make haste to help me, O Lord.

old: Now also when I am old and greyheaded, O God, forsake me not; until I have shewed thy strength unto this generation, and thy power to every one that is to come.
reftext: Now also when I am old and grayheaded, O God, forsake me not; until I have shewed thy strength unto this generation, and thy power to every one that is to come.

old: Give the king thy judgments, O God, and thy righteousness unto the king's son.
reftext: A Psalm for Solomon. Give the king thy judgments, O God, and thy righteousness unto the king’s son.

old: Truly God is good to Israel, even to such as are of a clean heart.
reftext: A Psalm of Asaph. Truly God is good to Israel, even to such as are of a clean heart.

old: O God, why hast thou cast us off for ever? why doth thine anger smoke against the sheep of thy pasture?
reftext: Maschil of Asaph. O God, why hast thou cast us off for ever? why doth thine anger smoke against the sheep of thy pasture?

old: Unto thee, O God, do we give thanks, unto thee do we give thanks: for that thy name is near thy wondrous works declare.
reftext: To the chief Musician, Al–taschith, A Psalm or Song of Asaph. Unto thee, O God, do we give thanks, unto thee do we give thanks: for that thy name is near thy wondrous works declare.

old: In Judah is God known: his name is great in Israel.
reftext: To the chief Musician on Neginoth, A Psalm or Song of Asaph. In Judah is God known: his name is great in Israel.

old: I cried unto God with my voice, even unto God with my voice; and he gave ear unto me.
reftext: To the chief Musician, to Jeduthun, A Psalm of Asaph. I cried unto God with my voice, even unto God with my voice; and he gave ear unto me.

old: Give ear, O my people, to my law: incline your ears to the words of my mouth.
reftext: Maschil of Asaph. Give ear, O my people, to my law: incline your ears to the words of my mouth.

old: O GOD, the heathen are come into thine inheritance; thy holy temple have they defiled; they have laid Jerusalem on heaps.
reftext: A Psalm of Asaph. O God, the heathen are come into thine inheritance; thy holy temple have they defiled; they have laid Jerusalem on heaps.

old: Give ear, O Shepherd of Israel, thou that leadest Joseph like a flock; thou that dwellest between the cherubims, shine forth.
reftext: To the chief Musician upon Shoshannim–Eduth, A Psalm of Asaph. Give ear, O Shepherd of Israel, thou that leadest Joseph like a flock; thou that dwellest between the cherubims, shine forth.

old: Sing aloud unto God our strength: make a joyful noise unto the God of Jacob.
reftext: To the chief Musician upon Gittith, A Psalm of Asaph. Sing aloud unto God our strength: make a joyful noise unto the God of Jacob.

old: God standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods.
reftext: A Psalm of Asaph. God standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods.

old: Keep not thou silence, O God: hold not thy peace, and be not still, O God.
reftext: A Song or Psalm of Asaph. Keep not thou silence, O God: hold not thy peace, and be not still, O God.

old: How amiable are thy tabernacles, O LORD of hosts!
reftext: To the chief Musician upon Gittith, A Psalm for the sons of Korah. How amiable are thy tabernacles, O Lord of hosts!

old: Lord, thou hast been favourable unto thy land: thou hast brought back the captivity of Jacob.
reftext: To the chief Musician, A Psalm for the sons of Korah. Lord, thou hast been favourable unto thy land: thou hast brought back the captivity of Jacob.

old: Bow down thine ear, O LORD, hear me: for I am poor and needy.
reftext: A Prayer of David. Bow down thine ear, O Lord, hear me: for I am poor and needy.

old: His foundation is in the holy mountains.
reftext: A Psalm or Song for the sons of Korah. His foundation is in the holy mountains.

old: O LORD God of my salvation, I have cried day and night before thee:
reftext: A Song or Psalm for the sons of Korah, to the chief Musician upon Mahalath Leannoth, Maschil of Heman the Ezrahite. O Lord God of my salvation, I have cried day and night before thee:

old: I will sing of the mercies of the LORD for ever: with my mouth will I make known thy faithfulness to all generations.
reftext: Maschil of Ethan the Ezrahite. I will sing of the mercies of the Lord for ever: with my mouth will I make known thy faithfulness to all generations.

old: Lord, thou hast been our dwelling place in all generations.
reftext: A Prayer of Moses the man of God. Lord, thou hast been our dwelling place in all generations.

old: IT IS A GOOD THING TO GIVE THANKS UNTO THE LORD, AND TO SING PRAISES UNTO THY NAME, O MOST HIGH:
reftext: A Psalm or Song for the sabbath day. It is a good thing to give thanks unto the Lord, and to sing praises unto thy name, O most High:

old: O sing unto the LORD a new song; for he hath done marvellous things: his right hand, and his holy arm, hath gotten him the victory.
reftext: A Psalm. O sing unto the Lord a new song; for he hath done marvellous things: his right hand, and his holy arm, hath gotten him the victory.

old: Make a joyful noise unto the LORD, all ye lands.
reftext: A Psalm of praise. Make a joyful noise unto the Lord, all ye lands.

old: I will sing of mercy and judgment: unto thee, O LORD, will I sing.
reftext: A Psalm of David. I will sing of mercy and judgment: unto thee, O Lord, will I sing.

old: Hear my prayer, O LORD, and let my cry come unto thee.
reftext: A Prayer of the afflicted, when he is overwhelmed, and poureth out his complaint before the Lord. Hear my prayer, O Lord, and let my cry come unto thee.

old: Bless the LORD, O my soul: and all that is within me, bless his holy name.
reftext: A Psalm of David. Bless the Lord, O my soul: and all that is within me, bless his holy name.

old: O God, my heart is fixed; I will sing and give praise, even with my glory.
reftext: A Song or Psalm of David. O God, my heart is fixed; I will sing and give praise, even with my glory.

old: Hold not thy peace, O God of my praise;
reftext: To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David. Hold not thy peace, O God of my praise;

old: The LORD said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool.
reftext: A Psalm of David. The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool.

old: Blessed are the undefiled in the way, who walk in the law of the LORD.
reftext: א ALEPH. Blessed are the undefiled in the way, who walk in the law of the Lord.

old: Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word.
reftext: ב BETH. Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word.

old: Deal bountifully with thy servant, that I may live, and keep thy word.
reftext: ג GIMEL. Deal bountifully with thy servant, that I may live, and keep thy word.

old: My soul cleaveth unto the dust: quicken thou me according to thy word.
reftext: ד DALETH. My soul cleaveth unto the dust: quicken thou me according to thy word.

old: Teach me, O LORD, the way of thy statutes; and I shall keep it unto the end.
reftext: ה HE. Teach me, O Lord, the way of thy statutes; and I shall keep it unto the end.

old: Let thy mercies come also unto me, O LORD, even thy salvation, according to thy word.
reftext: ו VAU. Let thy mercies come also unto me, O Lord, even thy salvation, according to thy word.

old: Remember the word unto thy servant, upon which thou hast caused me to hope.
reftext: ז ZAIN. Remember the word unto thy servant, upon which thou hast caused me to hope.

old: Thou art my portion, O LORD: I have said that I would keep thy words.
reftext: ח CHETH. Thou art my portion, O Lord: I have said that I would keep thy words.

old: Thou hast dealt well with thy servant, O LORD, according unto thy word.
reftext: ט TETH. Thou hast dealt well with thy servant, O Lord, according unto thy word.

old: Thy hands have made me and fashioned me: give me understanding, that I may learn thy commandments.
reftext: י JOD. Thy hands have made me and fashioned me: give me understanding, that I may learn thy commandments.

old: My soul fainteth for thy salvation: but I hope in thy word.
reftext: כ CAPH. My soul fainteth for thy salvation: but I hope in thy word.

old: For ever, O LORD, thy word is settled in heaven.
reftext: ל LAMED. For ever, O Lord, thy word is settled in heaven.

old: O how love I thy law! it is my meditation all the day.
reftext: מ MEM. O how love I thy law! it is my meditation all the day.

old: Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.
reftext: נ NUN. Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.

old: I hate vain thoughts: but thy law do I love.
reftext: ס SAMECH. I hate vain thoughts: but thy law do I love.

old: I have done judgment and justice: leave me not to mine oppressors.
reftext: ע AIN. I have done judgment and justice: leave me not to mine oppressors.

old: Thy testimonies are wonderful: therefore doth my soul keep them.
reftext: פ PE. Thy testimonies are wonderful: therefore doth my soul keep them.

old: Righteous art thou, O LORD, and upright are thy judgments.
reftext: צ TZADDI. Righteous art thou, O Lord, and upright are thy judgments.

old: I cried with my whole heart; hear me, O LORD: I will keep thy statutes.
reftext: ק KOPH. I cried with my whole heart; hear me, O Lord: I will keep thy statutes.

old: Consider mine affliction, and deliver me: for I do not forget thy law.
reftext: ר RESH. Consider mine affliction, and deliver me: for I do not forget thy law.

old: Princes have persecuted me without a cause: but my heart standeth in awe of thy word.
reftext: ש SCHIN. Princes have persecuted me without a cause: but my heart standeth in awe of thy word.

old: Let my cry come near before thee, O LORD: give me understanding according to thy word.
reftext: ת TAU. Let my cry come near before thee, O Lord: give me understanding according to thy word.

old: In my distress I cried unto the LORD, and he heard me.
reftext: A Song of degrees. In my distress I cried unto the Lord, and he heard me.

old: I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help.
reftext: A Song of degrees. I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help.

old: I was glad when they said unto me, Let us go into the house of the LORD.
reftext: A Song of degrees of David. I was glad when they said unto me, Let us go into the house of the Lord.

old: Unto thee lift I up mine eyes, O thou that dwellest in the heavens.
reftext: A Song of degrees. Unto thee lift I up mine eyes, O thou that dwellest in the heavens.

old: If it had not been the LORD who was on our side, now may Israel say;
reftext: A Song of degrees of David. If it had not been the Lord who was on our side, now may Israel say;

old: They that trust in the LORD shall be as mount Zion, which cannot be removed, but abideth for ever.
reftext: A Song of degrees. They that trust in the Lord shall be as mount Zion, which cannot be removed, but abideth for ever.

old: When the LORD turned again the captivity of Zion, we were like them that dream.
reftext: A Song of degrees. When the Lord turned again the captivity of Zion, we were like them that dream.

old: Except the LORD build the house, they labour in vain that build it: except the LORD keep the city, the watchman waketh but in vain.
reftext: A Song of degrees for Solomon. Except the Lord build the house, they labour in vain that build it: except the Lord keep the city, the watchman waketh but in vain.

old: Blessed is every one that feareth the LORD; that walketh in his ways.
reftext: A Song of degrees. Blessed is every one that feareth the Lord; that walketh in his ways.

old: Many a time have they afflicted me from my youth, may Israel now say:
reftext: A Song of degrees. Many a time have they afflicted me from my youth, may Israel now say:

old: Out of the depths have I cried unto thee, O LORD.
reftext: A Song of degrees. Out of the depths have I cried unto thee, O Lord.

old: Lord, my heart is not haughty, nor mine eyes lofty: neither do I exercise myself in great matters, or in things too high for me.
reftext: A Song of degrees of David. Lord, my heart is not haughty, nor mine eyes lofty: neither do I exercise myself in great matters, or in things too high for me.

old: Lord, remember David, and all his afflictions:
reftext: A Song of degrees. Lord, remember David, and all his afflictions:

old: Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!
reftext: A Song of degrees of David. Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!

old: Behold, bless ye the LORD, all ye servants of the LORD, which by night stand in the house of the LORD.
reftext: A Song of degrees. Behold, bless ye the Lord, all ye servants of the Lord, which by night stand in the house of the Lord.

old: I will praise thee with my whole heart: before the gods will I sing praise unto thee.
reftext: A Psalm of David. I will praise thee with my whole heart: before the gods will I sing praise unto thee.

old: O LORD, thou hast searched me, and known me.
reftext: To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David. O Lord, thou hast searched me, and known me.

old: Deliver me, O LORD, from the evil man: preserve me from the violent man;
reftext: To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David. Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man: preserve me from the violent man;

old: Lord, I cry unto thee: make haste unto me; give ear unto my voice, when I cry unto thee.
reftext: A Psalm of David. Lord, I cry unto thee: make haste unto me; give ear unto my voice, when I cry unto thee.

old: I cried unto the LORD with my voice; with my voice unto the LORD did I make my supplication.
reftext: Maschil of David; A Prayer when he was in the cave. I cried unto the Lord with my voice; with my voice unto the Lord did I make my supplication.

old: Hear my prayer, O LORD, give ear to my supplications: in thy faithfulness answer me, and in thy righteousness.
reftext: A Psalm of David. Hear my prayer, O Lord, give ear to my supplications: in thy faithfulness answer me, and in thy righteousness.

old: Blessed be the LORD my strength, which teacheth my hands to war, and my fingers to fight:
reftext: A Psalm of David. Blessed be the Lord my strength, which teacheth my hands to war, and my fingers to fight:

old: I will extol thee, my God, O king; and I will bless thy name for ever and ever.
reftext: David’s Psalm of praise. I will extol thee, my God, O king; and I will bless thy name for ever and ever.

old: Fire, and hail; snow, and vapours; stormy wind fulfilling his word:
reftext: Fire, and hail; snow, and vapour; stormy wind fulfilling his word:

old: The glory of young men is their strength: and the beauty of old men is the grey head.
reftext: The glory of young men is their strength: and the beauty of old men is the gray head.

old: Then I beheld all the work of God, that a man cannot find out the work that is done under the sun: because though a man labour to seek it out, yet he shall not find it; yea farther; though a wise man think to know it, yet shall he not be able to find it.
reftext: Then I beheld all the work of God, that a man cannot find out the work that is done under the sun: because though a man labour to seek it out, yet he shall not find it; yea further; though a wise man think to know it, yet shall he not be able to find it.

old: For he put on righteousness as a breastplate, and an helmet of salvation upon his head; and he put on the garments of vengeance for clothing, and was clad with zeal as a cloak.
reftext: For he put on righteousness as a breastplate, and an helmet of salvation upon his head; and he put on the garments of vengeance for clothing, and was clad with zeal as a cloke.

old: But ye turned and polluted my name, and caused every man his servant, and every man his handmaid, whom he had set at liberty at their pleasure, to return, and brought them into subjection, to be unto you for servants and for handmaids.
reftext: But ye turned and polluted my name, and caused every man his servant, and every man his handmaid, whom ye had set at liberty at their pleasure, to return, and brought them into subjection, to be unto you for servants and for handmaids.

old: The cedars in the garden of God could not hide him: the fir trees were not like his boughs, and the chestnut trees were not like his branches; nor any tree in the garden of God was like unto him in his beauty.
reftext: The cedars in the garden of God could not hide him: the fir trees were not like his boughs, and the chesnut trees were not like his branches; nor any tree in the garden of God was like unto him in his beauty.

old: And the floors shall be full of wheat, and the vats shall overflow with wine and oil.
reftext: And the floors shall be full of wheat, and the fats shall overflow with wine and oil.

old: But I will send a fire upon Moab, and it shall devour the palaces of Kirioth: and Moab shall die with tumult, with shouting, and with the sound of the trumpet:
reftext: But I will send a fire upon Moab, and it shall devour the palaces of Kerioth: and Moab shall die with tumult, with shouting, and with the sound of the trumpet:

old: Thou hast multiplied thy merchants above the stars of heaven: the cankerworm spoileth, and fleeth away.
reftext: Thou hast multiplied thy merchants above the stars of heaven: the cankerworm spoileth, and flieth away.

old: Now when Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judaea in the days of Herod the king, behold, there came wise men from the east to Jerusalem,
reftext: Now when Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of Herod the king, behold, there came wise men from the east to Jerusalem,

old: And they said unto him, In Bethlehem of Judaea: for thus it is written by the prophet,
reftext: And they said unto him, In Bethlehem of Judea: for thus it is written by the prophet,

old: But when he heard that Archelaus did reign in Judaea in the room of his father Herod, he was afraid to go thither: notwithstanding, being warned of God in a dream, he turned aside into the parts of Galilee:
reftext: But when he heard that Archelaus did reign in Judea in the room of his father Herod, he was afraid to go thither: notwithstanding, being warned of God in a dream, he turned aside into the parts of Galilee:

old: In those days came John the Baptist, preaching in the wilderness of Judaea,
reftext: In those days came John the Baptist, preaching in the wilderness of Judea,

old: Then went out to him Jerusalem, and all Judaea, and all the region round about Jordan,
reftext: Then went out to him Jerusalem, and all Judea, and all the region round about Jordan,

old: And there followed him great multitudes of people from Galilee, and from Decapolis, and from Jerusalem, and from Judaea, and from beyond Jordan.
reftext: And there followed him great multitudes of people from Galilee, and from Decapolis, and from Jerusalem, and from Judea, and from beyond Jordan.

old: And if any man will sue thee at the law, and take away thy coat, let him have thy cloak also.
reftext: And if any man will sue thee at the law, and take away thy coat, let him have thy cloke also.

old: Philip, and Bartholomew; Thomas, and Matthew the publican; James the son of Alphaeus, and Lebbaeus, whose surname was Thaddaeus;
reftext: Philip, and Bartholomew; Thomas, and Matthew the publican; James the son of Alpheus, and Lebbeus, whose surname was Thaddeus;

old: When Jesus came into the coasts of Caesarea Philippi, he asked his disciples, saying, Whom do men say that I the Son of man am?
reftext: When Jesus came into the coasts of Cesarea Philippi, he asked his disciples, saying, Whom do men say that I the Son of man am?

old: And it came to pass, that when Jesus had finished these sayings, he departed from Galilee, and came into the coasts of Judaea beyond Jordan;
reftext: And it came to pass, that when Jesus had finished these sayings, he departed from Galilee, and came into the coasts of Judea beyond Jordan;

old: Tell us therefore, What thinkest thou? Is it lawful to give tribute unto Caesar, or not?
reftext: Tell us therefore, What thinkest thou? Is it lawful to give tribute unto Cesar, or not?

old: They say unto him, Caesar's. Then saith he unto them, Render therefore unto Caesar the things which are Caesar's; and unto God the things that are God's.
reftext: They say unto him, Cesar’s. Then saith he unto them, Render therefore unto Cesar the things which are Cesar’s; and unto God the things that are God’s.

old: Then let them which be in Judaea flee into the mountains:
reftext: Then let them which be in Judea flee into the mountains:

old: And he went a little farther, and fell on his face, and prayed, saying, O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt.
reftext: And he went a little further, and fell on his face, and prayed, saying, O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt.

old: When the even was come, there came a rich man of Arimathaea, named Joseph, who also himself was Jesus' disciple:
reftext: When the even was come, there came a rich man of Arimathea, named Joseph, who also himself was Jesus’ disciple:

old: And there went out unto him all the land of Judaea, and they of Jerusalem, and were all baptized of him in the river of Jordan, confessing their sins.
reftext: And there went out unto him all the land of Judea, and they of Jerusalem, and were all baptized of him in the river of Jordan, confessing their sins.

old: And when he had gone a little farther thence, he saw James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, who also were in the ship mending their nets.
reftext: And when he had gone a little further thence, he saw James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, who also were in the ship mending their nets.

old: And as he passed by, he saw Levi the son of Alphaeus sitting at the receipt of custom, and said unto him, Follow me. And he arose and followed him.
reftext: And as he passed by, he saw Levi the son of Alpheus sitting at the receipt of custom, and said unto him, Follow me. And he arose and followed him.

old: But Jesus withdrew himself with his disciples to the sea: and a great multitude from Galilee followed him, and from Judaea,
reftext: But Jesus withdrew himself with his disciples to the sea: and a great multitude from Galilee followed him, and from Judea,

old: And from Jerusalem, and from Idumaea, and from beyond Jordan; and they about Tyre and Sidon, a great multitude, when they had heard what great things he did, came unto him.
reftext: And from Jerusalem, and from Idumea, and from beyond Jordan; and they about Tyre and Sidon, a great multitude, when they had heard what great things he did, came unto him.

old: And Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus, and Simon the Canaanite,
reftext: And Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James the son of Alpheus, and Thaddeus, and Simon the Canaanite,

old: And Jesus went out, and his disciples, into the towns of Caesarea Philippi: and by the way he asked his disciples, saying unto them, Whom do men say that I am?
reftext: And Jesus went out, and his disciples, into the towns of Cesarea Philippi: and by the way he asked his disciples, saying unto them, Whom do men say that I am?

old: And he arose from thence, and cometh into the coasts of Judaea by the farther side of Jordan: and the people resort unto him again; and, as he was wont, he taught them again.
reftext: And he arose from thence, and cometh into the coasts of Judea by the farther side of Jordan: and the people resort unto him again; and, as he was wont, he taught them again.

old: And they came to Jericho: and as he went out of Jericho with his disciples and a great number of people, blind Bartimaeus, the son of Timaeus, sat by the highway side begging.
reftext: And they came to Jericho: and as he went out of Jericho with his disciples and a great number of people, blind Bartimeus, the son of Timeus, sat by the highway side begging.

old: And when they were come, they say unto him, Master, we know that thou art true, and carest for no man: for thou regardest not the person of men, but teachest the way of God in truth: Is it lawful to give tribute to Caesar, or not?
reftext: And when they were come, they say unto him, Master, we know that thou art true, and carest for no man: for thou regardest not the person of men, but teachest the way of God in truth: Is it lawful to give tribute to Cesar, or not?

old: And they brought it. And he saith unto them, Whose is this image and superscription? And they said unto him, Caesar's.
reftext: And they brought it. And he saith unto them, Whose is this image and superscription? And they said unto him, Cesar’s.

old: And Jesus answering said unto them, Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's. And they marvelled at him.
